# Common Industriual Protocol (CIP)

The Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) is an object-oriented peer-to-peer protocol that enables connections between industrial devices (sensors, actuators) and higher-level devices (controllers). CIP is independent of physical media and the data link layer. CIP has two main purposes: transport of control-oriented data connected to I/O devices, and transport of information relating to the system to be controlled, such as configuration parameters or diagnostics.

CIP uses abstract objects to describe a device. A CIP device consists of a group of objects. Objects describe the available communication services, the externally visible behavior of the device, and a way in which information can be retrieved and exchanged. CIP objects are divided into classes, instances and attributes. A class is a set of objects that all represent the same component. An instance is the current representation of a particular object. Each instance has the same attributes, but possibly with different attribute values. The individual objects are addressed via a node address, which for EtherNet/IP is the IP address, plus a class, instance and attributes.

- Object

- An abstract representation of a particular component within a product.

- Class

- A set of objects that all represent the same type of system component. A class is a generalization of an object. All objects in a class are identical in form and behavior, but can contain different attribute values.

- Instance

- A specific and real specimen of an object.
  Example: Berlin is an instance of the Capital object class.

- Attribute

- A description of a property or characteristic of an object. Typically, attributes provide status information or control the operation of an object.

Un PLC ejecuta lógica de control de forma repetitiva y predecible. En lugar de cablear cada decisión con
relés, el comportamiento se expresa en software. Beckhoff lleva esta idea al PC-Based Control: un
computador industrial puede ejecutar control PLC, motion, comunicaciones y otras funciones de
automatización.

TwinCAT significa The Windows Control and Automation Technology. TwinCAT 3 integra la ingeniería en
un entorno basado en Visual Studio y separa conceptualmente el entorno de desarrollo del entorno que
ejecuta la aplicación de control.

Vista simplificada de la separación entre ingeniería y ejecución.

# Introduction

The method of emulating classic automation devices such as programmable logic controllers (PLC) and numerical controllers (NC) as software on powerful standard hardware has been the state of the art for many years and is now practiced by many manufacturers.

There are many benefits, but the most important is without doubt the fact that the software is mostly hardware-independent. This means, firstly, that the performance of the hardware can be specially adapted to the application and, secondly, that you can automatically benefit from its further development.

This particularly applies to PC hardware, whose performance is still increasingly at a dramatically fast rate. The relative independence from a supplier that results from this separation of software and hardware is also very important for the user.

Since the PLC and Motion Control – and possibly other automation components – remain independent logic function blocks with this method, there are only a few changes in the application architecture in comparison with classic automation technology.

The PLC determines the machine's logical processes and transfers the implementation of certain axis functions to the Motion Control. On account of the improved performance of the controllers and the possibility to use higher-level programming languages (IEC 61131-3), even complex machines can be automated in this way.

Uno de los mensajes importantes de esta serie ha sido que muchas prácticas provenientes del desarrollo de software tradicional también pueden aplicarse al mundo PLC.

Por ejemplo:

```text id="jzhwkd"
Software tradicional
       │
       ├── Git
       ├── Unit Testing
       ├── TDD
       ├── OOP
       ├── CI/CD
       └── Arquitectura modular
               │
               ▼
      Automatización industrial
```

No existe ninguna razón para que el software PLC tenga estándares de calidad inferiores.

\## Introducción a TwinCAT


Ahora avancemos algunas décadas hasta llegar al tema principal de este tutorial: \*\*TwinCAT\*\*.


TwinCAT significa:


\*\*The Windows Control and Automation Technology\*\*.


Beckhoff, la empresa responsable de TwinCAT, fue fundada en 1980 en Verl, Alemania, y desde sus inicios ha trabajado en el área de la automatización.


Una de las ideas principales de negocio de Beckhoff ha sido el concepto de \*\*control basado en PC\*\*, conocido como PC-Based Control.


Durante la década de 1980, Beckhoff comenzó a desarrollar sistemas de control basados en computadores estándar que ejecutaban DOS.


Esto representó un cambio importante dentro del mercado de los PLC, ya que otros fabricantes dependían en mayor medida de hardware y software propietarios.


En 1996, Beckhoff lanzó \*\*TwinCAT 2\*\*.


TwinCAT 2 permitía convertir un computador convencional basado en PC y ejecutando Windows en un controlador con capacidades de tiempo real.


Esto se conseguía permitiendo que el kernel de TwinCAT tuviera acceso directo al hardware para ejecutar todas las tareas críticas de tiempo real, mientras que Windows se utilizaba para ejecutar las aplicaciones de usuario.


Como muchos otros fabricantes de PLC, Beckhoff creó su propio entorno de desarrollo integrado, o IDE, en el cual era posible programar el software del PLC.


Junto con este IDE se instalaba también un \*\*System Manager\*\*, mediante el cual se realizaba toda la configuración del PLC.


\## Aparición de TwinCAT 3


En 2012, TwinCAT 3 fue lanzado públicamente.


Con TwinCAT 3, Beckhoff integró tanto el entorno de desarrollo como las funcionalidades del System Manager dentro de \*\*Microsoft Visual Studio\*\*.

# Common Industriual Protocol (CIP)

The Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) is an object-oriented peer-to-peer protocol that enables connections between industrial devices (sensors, actuators) and higher-level devices (controllers). CIP is independent of physical media and the data link layer. CIP has two main purposes: transport of control-oriented data connected to I/O devices, and transport of information relating to the system to be controlled, such as configuration parameters or diagnostics.

CIP uses abstract objects to describe a device. A CIP device consists of a group of objects. Objects describe the available communication services, the externally visible behavior of the device, and a way in which information can be retrieved and exchanged. CIP objects are divided into classes, instances and attributes. A class is a set of objects that all represent the same component. An instance is the current representation of a particular object. Each instance has the same attributes, but possibly with different attribute values. The individual objects are addressed via a node address, which for EtherNet/IP is the IP address, plus a class, instance and attributes.

- Object

- An abstract representation of a particular component within a product.

- Class

- A set of objects that all represent the same type of system component. A class is a generalization of an object. All objects in a class are identical in form and behavior, but can contain different attribute values.

- Instance

- A specific and real specimen of an object.
  Example: Berlin is an instance of the Capital object class.

- Attribute

- A description of a property or characteristic of an object. Typically, attributes provide status information or control the operation of an object.

This scenario describes the conventional implementation of OPC Servers. Servers using the old OPC A technology were often implemented on a central server instead of the Industrial PC on which TwinCAT runtime was executed, in order to avoid DCOM configurations. (Remember: in contrast to OPC UA, OPC DA is based on COM/DCOM technologies)

- TwinCAT 3 ADS (or TwinCAT 2 CP) for the required ADS connectivity

- Symbol files from any remote TwinCAT runtime
- OPC UA Client, which can be an HMI, MES or ERP system, for example.

\## Introducción a TwinCAT


Ahora avancemos algunas décadas hasta llegar al tema principal de este tutorial: \*\*TwinCAT\*\*.


TwinCAT significa:


\*\*The Windows Control and Automation Technology\*\*.


Beckhoff, la empresa responsable de TwinCAT, fue fundada en 1980 en Verl, Alemania, y desde sus inicios ha trabajado en el área de la automatización.


Una de las ideas principales de negocio de Beckhoff ha sido el concepto de \*\*control basado en PC\*\*, conocido como PC-Based Control.


Durante la década de 1980, Beckhoff comenzó a desarrollar sistemas de control basados en computadores estándar que ejecutaban DOS.


Esto representó un cambio importante dentro del mercado de los PLC, ya que otros fabricantes dependían en mayor medida de hardware y software propietarios.


En 1996, Beckhoff lanzó \*\*TwinCAT 2\*\*.


TwinCAT 2 permitía convertir un computador convencional basado en PC y ejecutando Windows en un controlador con capacidades de tiempo real.


Esto se conseguía permitiendo que el kernel de TwinCAT tuviera acceso directo al hardware para ejecutar todas las tareas críticas de tiempo real, mientras que Windows se utilizaba para ejecutar las aplicaciones de usuario.


Como muchos otros fabricantes de PLC, Beckhoff creó su propio entorno de desarrollo integrado, o IDE, en el cual era posible programar el software del PLC.


Junto con este IDE se instalaba también un \*\*System Manager\*\*, mediante el cual se realizaba toda la configuración del PLC.


\## Aparición de TwinCAT 3


En 2012, TwinCAT 3 fue lanzado públicamente.


Con TwinCAT 3, Beckhoff integró tanto el entorno de desarrollo como las funcionalidades del System Manager dentro de \*\*Microsoft Visual Studio\*\*.

# Introduction

The method of emulating classic automation devices such as programmable logic controllers (PLC) and numerical controllers (NC) as software on powerful standard hardware has been the state of the art for many years and is now practiced by many manufacturers.

There are many benefits, but the most important is without doubt the fact that the software is mostly hardware-independent. This means, firstly, that the performance of the hardware can be specially adapted to the application and, secondly, that you can automatically benefit from its further development.

This particularly applies to PC hardware, whose performance is still increasingly at a dramatically fast rate. The relative independence from a supplier that results from this separation of software and hardware is also very important for the user.

Since the PLC and Motion Control – and possibly other automation components – remain independent logic function blocks with this method, there are only a few changes in the application architecture in comparison with classic automation technology.

The PLC determines the machine's logical processes and transfers the implementation of certain axis functions to the Motion Control. On account of the improved performance of the controllers and the possibility to use higher-level programming languages (IEC 61131-3), even complex machines can be automated in this way.

Un PLC ejecuta lógica de control de forma repetitiva y predecible. En lugar de cablear cada decisión con
relés, el comportamiento se expresa en software. Beckhoff lleva esta idea al PC-Based Control: un
computador industrial puede ejecutar control PLC, motion, comunicaciones y otras funciones de
automatización.

TwinCAT significa The Windows Control and Automation Technology. TwinCAT 3 integra la ingeniería en
un entorno basado en Visual Studio y separa conceptualmente el entorno de desarrollo del entorno que
ejecuta la aplicación de control.

# Introduction

The method of emulating classic automation devices such as programmable logic controllers (PLC) and numerical controllers (NC) as software on powerful standard hardware has been the state of the art for many years and is now practiced by many manufacturers.

There are many benefits, but the most important is without doubt the fact that the software is mostly hardware-independent. This means, firstly, that the performance of the hardware can be specially adapted to the application and, secondly, that you can automatically benefit from its further development.

This particularly applies to PC hardware, whose performance is still increasingly at a dramatically fast rate. The relative independence from a supplier that results from this separation of software and hardware is also very important for the user.

Since the PLC and Motion Control – and possibly other automation components – remain independent logic function blocks with this method, there are only a few changes in the application architecture in comparison with classic automation technology.

The PLC determines the machine's logical processes and transfers the implementation of certain axis functions to the Motion Control. On account of the improved performance of the controllers and the possibility to use higher-level programming languages (IEC 61131-3), even complex machines can be automated in this way.

## Structure of the library

In contrast to the NC, the library functions work entirely in the PLC runtime. This has several consequences, which are listed below.

- Internal function blocks are usually also visible. This makes the online view less transparent. On the other hand, local variables can be used for an analysis.
- All parameters and even runtime variables are visible and accessible. This creates opportunities for specific manipulations. It should be obvious why this should be done with the utmost care.
- Nothing is done without a corresponding function block being called directly or indirectly. In contrast to the NC, the internal operation of the Motion Control is very transparent. This is particularly true for:

- Loading and saving of parameters.
- Recording of actual values.
- Setpoint generator.
- Regulation.
- Output adjustment.

- In contrast to NC, there are no "finished" axes. This increases the initial effort, but also offers opportunities for realizing adapted properties.
- Since the axis is configured in the PLC application, it is easily possible that unexpected and difficult to comprehend effects are created by an incorrect sequence or combination of the called function blocks. It is highly advisable to follow the examples.
- Since the function blocks are called by the PLC, the Motion Control also works with the cycle time of the PLC task. A task with a typical NC cycle time of considerably less than 10 ms should be used.

\# Programación de PLC utilizando TwinCAT 3 – Conceptos básicos e instalación


La automatización industrial existe desde mucho antes de que se inventaran los PLC.


Antes de los PLC, era posible automatizar un proceso utilizando sistemas de control basados en relés. Sin embargo, este enfoque requería enormes cantidades de relés, cableado y espacio físico, lo que además hacía que estos sistemas fueran difíciles de mantener.


Un pequeño cambio en el sistema podía requerir volver a cablear una parte importante de la instalación, y la rotura de un solo cable podía provocar que todo el sistema dejara de funcionar.


Durante la década de 1960 comenzaron a surgir las primeras ideas para reemplazar estos sistemas de control cableados mediante relés.


En esa década, de manera independiente, las empresas Allen-Bradley y General Motors investigaron alternativas electrónicas para reemplazar los sistemas de relés cableados, dando origen a los primeros PLC.


El primer PLC fue el \*\*Modicon Model 084\*\*, entregado en 1969.


Este PLC estaba compuesto por una placa de procesador, memoria y una placa denominada “logic solver”, encargada de interpretar los algoritmos asociados a la lógica Ladder.


Sin embargo, el Modicon 084 no tuvo éxito debido a diferentes razones, entre ellas su baja velocidad y la ausencia de algunas funcionalidades importantes.


En 1973 se lanzó el \*\*Modicon 184\*\*, considerado el primer PLC exitoso comercializado de forma masiva.


\## Introducción a TwinCAT


Ahora avancemos algunas décadas hasta llegar al tema principal de este tutorial: \*\*TwinCAT\*\*.


TwinCAT significa:


\*\*The Windows Control and Automation Technology\*\*.

Windows por sí solo no garantiza que una instrucción de usuario se ejecute exactamente cada cierto
intervalo. En control industrial, en cambio, el momento de leer sensores, calcular la lógica y actualizar
actuadores puede ser tan importante como el resultado lógico.

como tiempo de ciclo, prioridad y afinidad de CPU. El código PLC asignado a la tarea se ejecuta conforme
a ese ciclo.

El código creado en XAE se ejecuta en el runtime XAR bajo tareas de tiempo real.

# Triggered analysis of a time period

## Motivation

In addition to the continuous time analysis of a process, e.g. the vibration behavior of a continuously rotating shaft, another frequent application is the analysis of a defined timeframe. Application examples include analysis of vibration signals on a drill head, a milling unit or a shaft which only rotates during certain periods of time.

The advantage of an analysis integrated into the controller is particularly apparent in this case. The control usually initiates a certain process step, e.g. drilling. Accordingly, the sequential machine control can be used to trigger not only the process step but also the corresponding analysis step.

Application examples include analysis of vibration signals on a drill head, a milling unit or a shaft which only rotates during certain periods of time.

The advantage of an analysis integrated into the controller is particularly apparent in this case. The control usually initiates a certain process step, e.g. drilling. Accordingly, the sequential machine control can be used to trigger not only the process step but also the corresponding analysis step.

## Modularization

In order to master the complexity of modern machines and at the same time to reduce the necessary engineering expenditure, many machine manufacturers have begun to modularize their machines. Individual functions, assemblies or machine units are thereby regarded as modules, which are as independent as possible and are embedded into the overall system via uniform interfaces.

Ideally a machine is then structured hierarchically, whereby the lowest modules represent the simplest, continually reusable basic elements. Joined together they form increasingly complex machine units, up to the highest level where the entire machine is created. Different approaches are followed when it comes to the control system aspects of machine modularization. These can be roughly divided into a decentralized and a centralized approach.

In the local approach, each machine module is given its own controller, which determines the PLC functions and possibly also the motion functions of the module.

The individual modules can be put into operation and maintained separately from one another and scaled relatively independently. The necessary interactions between the controllers are coordinated via communication networks (fieldbuses or Ethernet) and standardized via appropriate profiles.

The central approach concentrates all control functions of all modules in the common controller and uses only very little pre-processing intelligence in the local I/O devices. The interactions can occur much more directly within the central control unit, as the communication paths become much shorter. Dead times do not occur and use of the control hardware is much more balanced, which reduces overall costs.

# Cómo funciona un ciclo EtherCAT

Podemos imaginar el telegrama EtherCAT como un tren extremadamente rápido.

El PLC genera datos de salida.

Estos datos contienen información para los actuadores.

El telegrama comienza a recorrer la red.

Cuando llega al primer EtherCAT Slave:

* entrega la información de salida destinada a ese dispositivo;
* recoge los datos de entrada disponibles.

Los datos de entrada normalmente proceden de sensores.

El telegrama continúa hasta el siguiente slave.

El proceso se repite:

* entrega outputs;
* recoge inputs.

Después de pasar por todos los dispositivos, el telegrama vuelve al EtherCAT Master.

El PLC recibe entonces todos los datos actualizados de entrada.

### 4.1 Por qué importa el determinismo

Windows por sí solo no garantiza que una instrucción de usuario se ejecute exactamente cada cierto
intervalo. En control industrial, en cambio, el momento de leer sensores, calcular la lógica y actualizar
actuadores puede ser tan importante como el resultado lógico.

TwinCAT incorpora un entorno de tiempo real y tareas configurables. Una tarea dispone de parámetros
como tiempo de ciclo, prioridad y afinidad de CPU. El código PLC asignado a la tarea se ejecuta conforme
a ese ciclo.

El código creado en XAE se ejecuta en el runtime XAR bajo tareas de tiempo real.
